articles.author: johnettagaweraks
articles.description:
JWT-Secured Authorization Requests Need Their Own Replay Boundary


An OAuth authorization request is usually a URL full of query parameters. A browser user agent sees that URL, and intermediaries may see it too. RFC 9101 addresses this design weakness by placing the authorization request in a JSON Web Token called a Request Object. The result can be signed, encrypted, or both, and it can be sent by value in the request parameter or by reference through request_uri.
That change protects the request contents from casual alteration. It does not turn the authorization transaction into a one-time event. A signed Request Object can remain valid after its first presentation unless the authorization server ties it to a short-lived transaction, a client, and a single authorization attempt. Teams t…
articles.title: JWT-Secured Authorization Requests Need Their Own Replay Boundary

When a CI job reports that the Cypress binary is missing, it is not a download failure: the npm package installed correctly, and the binary is either sitting somewhere else on the same disk or was never carried between two jobs. Cypress keeps the binary in a global cache outside node_modules, so restoring node_modules without that cache produces this message every time.

The recorded run: the install wrote 819M of binary to one cache folder, the test step read another, and cypress install finished the job in the folder that was empty.

Two things install in two places. Every version of this failure is the second place going missing, and every fix is a way of making the two agree.

articles.author: lifeissoup
articles.description:
To run a cron job every day at midnight, use 0 0 * * *. That means minute 0, hour 0, every day of the month, every month, every day of the week. If you want to check a variation before deploying it, the Cron Expression Generator explains any 5-field expression in plain English and previews the next run times.
0 0 * * *
| | | | |
| | | | +-- day of week (0-7, Sunday is 0 or 7)
| | | +---- month (1-12)
| | +------ day of month (1-31)
| +-------- hour (0-23)
+---------- minute (0-59)

Hours use a 24-hour clock, so midnight is hour 0, not 12 and not 24. A full crontab line looks like this:
0 0 * * * /usr/local/bin/backup.sh >> /var/log/backup.log 2>&1

Edit your crontab with crontab -e. The >> ... 2>&1 part appends both stdout and stderr to a log file. Without it, cron tries to email the outpu…
articles.title: Cron Expression for Every Day at Midnight (0 0 * * *)

articles.author: Kay
articles.description:
A GitHub Actions if condition always runs when the value is a string with an expression inside it, such as if: ${{ github.ref }} == 'refs/heads/main': the runner turns the mixed value into a format() call, the result is non-empty text, and non-empty text is true. Put the whole condition inside one ${{ }}, or drop the markers entirely; quoting the condition is harmless and is not the cause.

Only the fourth and fifth rows build a format call. Everything else compiles to the comparison you meant, quoted or not.
A step or job that should be conditional runs on every event, every branch and every pull request. There is no error and no warning; the run is green and the guarded work simply happens when it should not. Inverting the condition does not help, because the inverse is also a non-empty …
